deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page continues a letter that is signed on the next page 'Göttingen, 12. Juni 1850 … dankbarer Schüler B. Riemann' and addressed to 'Ew. Hochwohlgeboren'. The subject is the Pfaff problem. The task is to transform a Pfaffian expression Omega = sum_{mu=0}^{n-1} p_mu dx_mu into e^t times a Pfaffian expression in one variable fewer. 'G. g. A. 1815 p. 1035' refers to the anonymous review of Pfaff's 'Methodus generalis…' in the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen. Jacobi took over a remark from that review in his 1827 Crelle paper on Pfaff's method. The review is by Gauss, so the addressee is almost certainly Gauss; this attribution is my inference.

Setup from the previous page, in modern form. Variables are x_0..x_{n-1} and an auxiliary t. Write (mu,nu) = dp_mu/dx_nu - dp_nu/dx_mu, a skew matrix A. A variation delta = (dx, dt) leaves e^{-t} Omega invariant iff the following n+1 equations hold:
  k_mu = sum_nu (mu,nu) dx_nu - p_mu dt = 0 (mu = 0..n-1),
  omega = sum p_mu dx_mu = 0.
This is system (A).

The footnote is Cartan's formula. In modern terms:
  L_delta(e^{-t}Omega) = i_delta d(e^{-t}Omega) + d(i_delta(e^{-t}Omega)) = e^{-t}(sum k_mu dx_mu + omega dt) + d(omega e^{-t}).
I checked this: i_delta dOmega = sum_mu dx_mu sum_nu (mu,nu) dx_nu, and i_delta(-dt ^ Omega) = -dt Omega + omega dt.

The identity is sum k_mu dx_mu + omega dt = 0. It holds because sum (mu,nu) dx_mu dx_nu = 0 by skewness, and the dt-terms cancel.

This page.
(1) Suppose some system of relations makes k_1, …, k_{n-1} and omega vanish. The identity then gives k_0 dx_0 = 0. Hence k_0 = 0 unless dx_0 = 0, i.e. unless the system implies x = const. Riemann notes that the condition 'not x = const' is identical with the review's demand that dx'/dx, …, dx^{(n-1)}/dx have finite values. It is also built into the review's system (B): omega/dx = 0, k_1 = … = k_{n-1} = 0. On this system the review makes the transformation depend.
(2) The review later substitutes system (C): k_0 = k_1 = … = k_{n-1} = 0. This is n homogeneous linear equations in (dx, dt). By the identity, (C) gives omega dt = 0. So omega = 0 follows only if dt ≠ 0. Hence (C) must be supplemented by the condition dt ≠ 0, not dx ≠ 0.
Implicit reasoning, mine: if dt = 0, (C) reduces to A dx = 0. For odd n the skew matrix A is always singular, so nonzero solutions with dt = 0 exist that need not satisfy omega = 0.
(3) Riemann prefers to start from (A) in the degenerate case, where some of the equations follow from the others (rank deficiency). In that case the review's rule must be restricted. The redundant equations of (C) may not be replaced by entirely arbitrary relations, only by relations chosen so that omega = 0 also holds. Since this is always possible, the transformation is executable for both even and odd n.

Modern summary. Riemann computes the infinitesimal conformal symmetries of Omega. Equivalently, he computes the Cauchy characteristic system of the form e^{-t}Omega in n+1 variables. He uses this to correct the treatment of the even/odd-n cases in Pfaff's method, as presented by Gauss and Jacobi.
errors: Calling (A) 'necessary' for invariance is slightly loose. Lie-derivative zero only requires i_delta d(e^{-t}Omega) + d(i_delta e^{-t}Omega) = 0, not each term separately. With omega = 0 imposed, as in the Pfaff method, the claim is correct.
The page contains no mathematical errors; the argument from the identity is sound.

The phrases 'always possible' and 'transformation executable for odd n' are asserted without proof. They rest on standard linear algebra plus integrability of the reduced system, which is not discussed here.

results.what: Cartan-type formula delta(Omega e^{-t}) = (sum k_mu dx_mu + omega dt) e^{-t} + d(omega e^{-t}), and the system k_mu = 0, omega = 0 (characteristic system of e^{-t}Omega).
results.modern_name: Cartan's magic formula / Cauchy characteristics of a Pfaffian form (conformal symmetry of a 1-form)
results.usually_credited_to: Pfaff 1815, Jacobi 1827 (Pfaff method); Cartan c.1899–1922 for the invariant formulation

results.what: Identity sum k_mu dx_mu + omega dt = 0 and its consequence: if k_1..k_{n-1}, omega vanish and dx ≠ 0, then k_0 = 0; if all k vanish and dt ≠ 0, then omega = 0.
results.modern_name: Skew-symmetry identity v^T A v = 0 / dependence of characteristic equations

results.what: Correction to the GGA 1815 review and to Jacobi: the substituted system (C) needs dt ≠ 0, not dx ≠ 0. In degenerate cases the redundant equations must be replaced compatibly with omega = 0, so the reduction works for both parities of n.
results.modern_name: Pfaff problem: reduction to normal form for even and odd class / rank of the skew matrix
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi, Clebsch, Frobenius (1877, full treatment of the Pfaff problem), Darboux 1882

deep.surprise_reason: A letter from the young Riemann (1850, probably to Gauss) correcting the Gauss review and Jacobi on the Pfaff problem is a notable unpublished biographical and mathematical detail. The e^{-t} device is in effect the Cauchy-characteristic or conformal-symmetry formulation, and the parity-independence remark is noteworthy. Still, the content is within the Pfaff–Jacobi framework of the time and is not a major new theorem.

checkable.sympy: n=4; x=symbols('x0:4'); p=[Function('p%d'%i)(*x) for i in range(n)]; dx=symbols('d0:4'); dt=symbols('dt'); A=Matrix(n,n,lambda i,j: diff(p[i],x[j])-diff(p[j],x[i])); k=[sum(A[i,j]*dx[j] for j in range(n))-p[i]*dt for i in range(n)]; w=sum(p[i]*dx[i] for i in range(n)); simplify(sum(k[i]*dx[i] for i in range(n))+w*dt)==0
checkable.asserts: The identity k dx + k' dx' + ... + omega dt = 0 (here n = 4).
An odd-order skew matrix (n = 3) is singular, so system (C) admits solutions with dt = 0; hence dt ≠ 0 must be required.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,d,e,f=symbols('a b c d e f'); simplify(Matrix([[0,a,b,c],[-a,0,d,e],[-b,-d,0,f],[-c,-e,-f,0]]).det()-(a*f-b*e+c*d)**2)==0
checkable.asserts: For even n the skew matrix is generically nonsingular (determinant = Pfaffian squared), which is why parity matters in the GGA treatment.

transcription_corrections: In (B) the image shows 'k' = σ' (a slipped 0); it should read k' = 0, as transcribed.
'G. g. A.' is the Göttingische gelehrte Anzeigen; the transcription is fine.

The underlinings in the image are not reflected in the transcription: 'so bald aus ihnen nicht folgt', 'daß δt, nicht die, daß δx', 'zugleich', 'sowohl bei geradem als ungeradem n die Transformation ausführbar'.
